title: You Can't Be Buried in This Town ❄️
desc:
In Longyearbyen, on Norway's Svalbard islands, the cemetery stopped accepting burials in 1950 — bodies in the permafrost weren't decomposing. Today, seriously ill residents are flown to mainland Norway.
📍 Longyearbyen, Svalbard, Norway
📚 Sources: Atlas Obscura · Polarpedia · The Guardian (2015)

title: The First Speeding Ticket Was for 8 MPH 🚗
desc:
On 28 January 1896 in Kent, England, Walter Arnold was fined one shilling for driving about 8 mph — four times the 2 mph town limit. He's said to have been chased down by a policeman on a bicycle. Later that year the limit rose to 14 mph.
📚 Sources: Guinness World Records · Historic UK · Wikipedia "Arnold (automobile)"
🎵 Music: "False Vacuum Decay" (YouTube Audio Library)

title: Octopuses Have 3 Hearts and Blue Blood 🐙
desc:
Two hearts pump blood through the gills, one pumps it to the rest of the body. The blood is blue because it carries oxygen with copper-based hemocyanin. The main heart stops beating when the octopus swims — and about two-thirds of its neurons are in its arms.
📚 Sources: Smithsonian Magazine · PBS Nature · National Aquarium
🎵 Music: "False Vacuum Decay" (YouTube Audio Library)

title: A Piece of India Inside Bangladesh Inside India Inside Bangladesh 🇮🇳🇧🇩
desc:
Dahala Khagrabari was the world's only third-order enclave: a field of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh. It disappeared in 2015, when India and Bangladesh swapped more than 160 enclaves. It's #1 in our video "The 8 Strangest Borders on Earth".
📍 Cooch Behar region, India–Bangladesh border
📚 Sources: Wikipedia "Dahala Khagrabari" · BBC

title: The Day an Entire Country Switched Sides of the Road 🇸🇪
desc:
On 3 September 1967 (Dagen H), Sweden switched from left- to right-hand traffic. At 4:50 a.m. every car stopped, moved to the right, and at 5:00 traffic resumed. About 350,000 road signs were changed — and the next Monday had fewer accidents than usual.
📚 Sources: Wikipedia "Dagen H" · Time (15 Sept 1967)
🎵 Music: "Red Shift" (YouTube Audio Library)

title: Why Flights to Tokyo Fly Over the Arctic ✈️
desc:
On a flat map, New York to Tokyo looks like a straight line across the Pacific. But planes fly north over Canada and Alaska — because on a round Earth the shortest path is a great circle, about 10,800 km instead of ~12,700 km.
📚 Sources: great-circle distances (Great Circle Mapper) · Encyclopaedia Britannica (great circle; Mercator projection)
🗺️ Map data: Natural Earth

title: The City That Couldn't Stop Dancing (1518) 💃
desc:
In July 1518 in Strasbourg, a woman began dancing in the street and couldn't stop. By late August, as many as 400 people were dancing. The city built a stage and hired musicians — which made it worse. Historian John Waller's leading theory: stress-induced mass hysteria.
📚 Sources: History.com · Popular Science (interview with John Waller)
🎵 Music: "Event Horizon" (YouTube Audio Library)

title: Greenland Isn't That Big. Your Map Lies. 🗺️
desc:
On the Mercator map Greenland looks as big as Africa — but Africa is about 14 times bigger (30.4M km² vs 2.2M km²). Mercator's 1569 projection stretches everything near the poles.
📚 Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica (Mercator projection; Greenland; Africa)

title: This Lake Holds More Water Than All 5 Great Lakes 🌊
desc:
Lake Baikal in Siberia is the deepest lake on Earth (1,642 m) and holds ~23,600 km³ of water — about a fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. It's ~25 million years old, the oldest lake in the world.
📚 Sources: Wikipedia "Lake Baikal" · WorldAtlas (USGS data)

title: Breakfast and Dinner at the Same Time? Only in Russia 🇷🇺
desc:
Russia spans 11 time zones, from Kaliningrad (UTC+2) to Kamchatka (UTC+12). The Trans-Siberian Railway from Moscow to Vladivostok is about 9,289 km and takes around 7 days.
📚 Sources: timeanddate.com · Encyclopaedia Britannica (Trans-Siberian Railroad)

title: Canada's Coastline Could Wrap Around Earth 6 Times 🇨🇦
desc:
Canada has the world's longest coastline: 243,042 km including its islands, touching the Pacific, Atlantic and Arctic. It has 52,455 islands. Norway is second with ~83,281 km.
📚 Sources: Statistics Canada · Guinness World Records

title: Australia Is Wider Than the Moon 🌕
desc:
The Moon is about 3,474 km across. Australia, from Steep Point to Cape Byron, is about 4,000 km wide. The Moon's surface (~37.9M km²) is still about 5× Australia's (7.7M km²).
📚 Sources: NASA Moon fact sheet · Geoscience Australia · Australian Bureau of Statistics
🗺️ Map data: Natural Earth

title: Everest Isn't the Tallest Mountain? It Depends 🏔️
desc:
Everest is highest above sea level (8,849 m). Mauna Kea is tallest from base to peak (over 10,200 m). And Chimborazo's summit is about 2 km farther from Earth's center than Everest's, because Earth bulges at the equator.
📚 Sources: NOAA Ocean Service · USGS
